description: baseline

Target launch overhead on n=32/176/352 with a Triton small-matrix QR path: one program handles one or several matrices, keeps full or partial columns in SRAM/registers, and emits torch.geqrf-compatible compact Householder output.
Initial Triton n=32 Householder path built but validation produced NaNs in H on the n=32 test.
Triton n=32 path fixed tau sign and avoided NaNs, but validation failed factor residual because compact H did not preserve upper-triangular R entries.
Triton n=32 path attempted to preserve compact R entries, but validation still failed because later reflector steps overwrote earlier upper rows with stale work values.
Triton n=32 compact-H path narrowed trailing R stores, but validation still failed the n=32 factor residual; next step is matching PyTorch geqrf sign convention exactly.
Triton n=32 path masked current-column H stores but validation still failed; diagnostic showed R row entries were double-subtracted due to store/load ordering in the trailing update.

Validated Triton n=32 Householder QR path with one program per matrix and compact geqrf-compatible H/tau; other sizes stay on torch.geqrf. Benchmark geomean improved from 116500.479 us to 107905.716 us.
Added dynamic-loop Triton Householder QR path for n=176 while keeping n=32 Triton and larger sizes on torch.geqrf; benchmark geomean improved to 101504.909 us.

Extended the dynamic-loop Triton Householder QR path to n=352. It validated but benchmark geomean regressed to 103907.517 us because the n=352 shape slowed versus torch.geqrf, so this path should not be kept as best.
Removed the slower n=352 Triton route and restored the best validated scope: Triton for n=32 and n=176, torch.geqrf otherwise. Revalidation passed; benchmark geomean measured 101538.223 us.
Reduced allocation overhead by using the cloned output H buffer as the Triton work buffer for n=32 and n=176. Validation passed; benchmark geomean improved slightly to 101343.383 us.

Brief exhausted. Best validated commit is 0550455aefea284d6d22704becaf24ae16f5940e with Triton Householder QR for n=32 and n=176, reusing the cloned H buffer, and torch.geqrf for larger sizes. Best unprofiled benchmark geomean reached 101343.383 us versus baseline 116500.479 us (~1.15x speedup). n=352 Triton also validated but regressed geomean, so it was removed; next useful briefs could explore blocked/tiled n=352 or n=512 instead of one-program full-column QR.

Profile the current best on n=352, then build a shape-specific Triton custom-kernel path that attacks launch/copy overhead from the failed n=352 attempt: fuse or remove redundant H-panel movement/update work, gate strictly to n=352, and preserve existing n=32/n=176/large-rankdef paths unless n=352 and geomean improve.

Added shape-specific split Triton n=352 QR path with separate reflector and parallel trailing-column update kernels. Validation passed and benchmark geomean improved to 83324.181 us, with n=352 dropping from ~39017 us to ~4892 us.
Widened the n=352 split-update Triton tile from 16 to 32 columns to reduce launch overhead. Validation passed and benchmark geomean improved to 83013.619 us; n=352 measured ~4689 us.
Increased n=352 split-update tile to 64 columns. Validation passed and benchmark geomean improved slightly to 82945.604 us; n=352 measured ~4696 us with fewer update launches.

Attempted to fuse n=352 reflector generation into the parallel update launches to remove the separate reflector kernel, but validation failed on n=352 factor residual, likely due to inter-CTA ordering between col_pid=0 stores and other column-block updates.
Attempted a 48-column n=352 update tile, but Triton requires tl.arange bounds to be powers of two and validation failed during JIT compilation before n=352 tests completed.

Brief exhausted. Best commit is 06fa26aa76703b16eb88b0e6cd0c0940e3f9f088 with a strictly n=352 Triton split QR path: one reflector kernel plus parallel trailing update kernels, while preserving n=32/n=176 Triton and existing large rank-def routes. Best validated benchmark geomean is 82945.604 us versus parent/profile around 100526 us and baseline 116500.479 us; n=352 dropped from ~39017 us to ~4696 us. A fused reflector/update attempt failed due to inter-CTA ordering, and a 48-column tile failed Triton arange power-of-two constraints; next briefs could explore a correctness-preserving single-CTA fused update or reduce n=32 launch overhead, which now dominates nsys.

Combine the global-best n=512 split-QR tile32 path with the n=352 tile64 update improvement, resolving dispatch conflicts while keeping the existing small-size and rankdef/nearrank shortcut paths intact so both improvements can stack.

Combined n=352 tile64 update with the n=512 tile32 split QR path. Build and validation passed, but the full benchmark timed out at 8 minutes, indicating stacked Triton paths are too slow/noisy under the full active benchmark.

Re-ran the combined n=352 tile64 plus n=512 tile32 split QR stack with a longer outer timeout to allow GPU-lock queueing. Validation remained clean and full benchmark succeeded with geomean 63188.190 us, stacking both parent improvements.

Tried resolving dispatch by checking the n>=512 rank-def shortcut before the n=512 split QR path. Validation passed, but benchmark regressed to 66812.006 us because the rankdef n=512 benchmark became much slower (~761 ms), so this ordering should be discarded.

Restored the best combined dispatch order after the rank-def-first experiment regressed: n=352 tile64, then n=512 batch640 split QR, then large rank-def/nearrank shortcuts. This returns to the validated 63188.190 us stack.

Brief exhausted. Successfully combined the global-best n=512 tile32 split QR path with the n=352 tile64 update path while keeping n=32/n=176 Triton and large rankdef/nearrank shortcuts intact. Best validated unprofiled benchmark is commit 5c401f77d664d111628ae0940e17a307b52c8c1d at 63188.190 us; final HEAD b6f7523d3c6bec3e8e570571f93c6e76f11ef65 restores the same best dispatch after a rankdef-first experiment. The rankdef-first dispatch validated but regressed to 66812.006 us because n=512 rankdef slowed to ~761 ms, so do not use it. Profiles were saved for both the best measured commit and final HEAD; next briefs should attack n=512 split path cost/launch count or the n=352 profiler slowdown under nsys.

Combine the global-best n=512 tile64 split-QR update path with the n=352 tile64 update improvement, preserving existing n=32/n=176 and rankdef/nearrank shortcuts while resolving dispatch conflicts and testing whether the n=352 specialization stacks cleanly.

Combined the n=352 tile64 update specialization with the n=512 tile64 split QR parent. Build and validation passed, including differential and invariance guards, but the full benchmark timed out at the 8-minute environment timeout, so this stacked tile64/tile64 dispatch is too slow/noisy as-is.

Re-ran the n=352 tile64 plus n=512 tile64 split QR stack with a longer outer timeout to avoid GPU-lock queueing. Validation was already clean; full benchmark succeeded at 61632.071 us, improving on the prior tile32/n352 stack and showing the tile64 parents stack cleanly. Saved an nsys profile for this commit.

Brief exhausted. Starting from the n=512 tile64 split-QR parent, I applied the n=352 tile64 update specialization from 06fa26aa so both requested parents stack in one dispatch: n=32/n=176 Triton paths, n=352 split QR tile64, n=512 batch640 split QR tile64, then existing large rankdef/nearrank shortcuts. The first full benchmark hit the 8-minute outer timeout after validation, so it was logged as runtime_error at commit 0a2c674a. Re-running the same validated commit with a longer queue-safe timeout succeeded at linalg/qr_v2=61632.071 us, better than the previous n352+n512 tile32 stack at 63188.190 us. An nsys profile was saved at autocuda/profiles/2026-06-24-09-38-31-qrv2_kernel_languages_m7w1ravpo/worker-0-brief-3-iteration-1-0a2c674a3cebbafa1bb8ff5a1cbf02c702c68e1b.nsys-rep. No further on-brief dispatch conflicts remain; future briefs should attack the dominant n=512 split QR launch/runtime or the n=32 overhead, not rankdef-first ordering (already regressed in brief 2).

Combine dispatch-specialized QR fast paths by stacking the current n=352 tile64 plus n=512 tile64 global-best with the validated n=1024 tile32 split path, fixing dispatch interference so n=352/n=512/n=1024 all route correctly while preserving n=32/n=176 and rankdef/nearrank shortcuts.

Stacked the validated n=1024 tile32 split QR path onto the n=352 tile64 plus n=512 tile64 global-best dispatch. Build, validation, differential, and invariance guards passed; full benchmark improved slightly to 61447.997 us while preserving n=32/n=176 and rankdef/nearrank shortcuts.

Brief exhausted. Starting from the n=352 tile64 plus n=512 tile64 global-best parent, I stacked the validated n=1024 tile32 split QR path from 5329fc62 while preserving n=32/n=176 dispatch and rankdef/nearrank shortcuts. The combined commit 4ae0a0d2e299aed5e296c149c5f469a38e3130b8 passed build, full validation, differential guard, and invariance guard, and benchmarked at linalg/qr_v2=61447.997 us versus the first parent at 61632.071 us. An nsys profile was saved at autocuda/profiles/2026-06-24-09-38-31-qrv2_kernel_languages_m7w1ravpo/worker-0-brief-4-iteration-0-4ae0a0d2e299aed5e296c149c5f469a38e3130b8.nsys-rep. No remaining on-brief dispatch conflicts were found; further work should target the dominant n=512 split QR path, the n=32 kernel overhead, or the n=1024 split path launch count/col-block structure.

Combine the n=512 fused two-reflector global-best path with the n=352 tile64 and n=1024 tile32 dispatch stack, resolving QR dispatch conflicts so n=512 keeps the fused path while n=352/n1024 and existing n=32/176/rankdef/nearrank shortcuts still route correctly.

Removed the now-unused single-reflector n=512 split QR kernels after the combine so dispatch has only the fused two-reflector n=512 path plus n=352 tile64 and n=1024 tile32 routes. Validation passed; benchmark was performance-neutral within noise.

Brief exhausted. The first parent already contained the requested n=512 fused two-reflector path stacked with n=352 tile64 and n=1024 tile32 dispatch, and direct validation/benchmark gave 49419.332 us. I committed a cleanup-only iteration fc8323d7 removing the unused single-reflector n=512 split kernels so dispatch cannot conflict; it validated and benchmarked at 49421.092 us, neutral within noise, and has an nsys profile. No further combine work remains under this brief; next useful direction is outside-brief, likely adopting worker1's later four-reflector n=512 path or reducing check/torch.geqrf-heavy large-shape overhead.

Combine the global-best n=512 quad-reflector fused QR path with the n=352 tile64 and n=1024 tile32 size-dispatch stack, preserving existing n=32/n=176 and rankdef/nearrank shortcuts while making dispatch precedence route n=512 to quad, n=352 to tile64, and n=1024 to tile32.

Combined the n=512 quad-reflector fused QR parent with the n=352 tile64 and n=1024 tile32 dispatch stack, then removed stale single- and pair-reflector n512 paths so n512 can only route to quad while n352/n1024 and rankdef/nearrank shortcuts remain intact. Build, validation, differential/invariance guards, benchmark, and nsys profile completed.

Brief exhausted. Combined the global-best n=512 quad-reflector fused QR path with the n=352 tile64 and n=1024 tile32 dispatch stack at commit cee4efe332fe24e880f184696c111fad0fcf0d79. The branch now routes n=512 batch640 to quad, n=352 to tile64 split QR, n=1024 to tile32 split QR after the rankdef/nearrank guards where applicable, and preserves n=32/n=176 paths. I removed unused single- and pair-reflector n512 kernels to avoid stale dispatch conflicts. Build, full validation, differential/invariance guards, benchmark, and nsys profile passed; best benchmark was linalg/qr_v2=39564.618 us, with profile saved under autocuda/profiles/2026-06-24-09-38-31-qrv2_kernel_languages_m7w1ravpo/worker-0-brief-6-iteration-0-cee4efe332fe24e880f184696c111fad0fcf0d79.nsys-rep. No further on-brief combine work remains; next useful briefs should attack n=512 quad runtime/launch count, n=1024 launch count, or large-shape torch.geqrf fallback/shortcut opportunities.

Profile the n=1024 path, then reduce launch count with a custom Triton fused two-reflector update kernel, expanding toward quad-fused only if register pressure and occupancy stay healthy. Route only n=1024 through this path while preserving existing n=32/n=512 behavior and the current dispatch split.

Added an n=1024 two-reflector Triton path that fuses adjacent Householder updates while preserving existing n=32/n=512 dispatch behavior. Validation passed and benchmark geomean improved to 34582.572 us, with dense/mixed n=1024 shapes around 96.1 ms.

Attempted to expand n=1024 QR from pair-fused to quad-fused Triton reflector/update kernels. Build passed, but validation failed dense/clustered/mixed n=1024 factor residuals, indicating the quad panel update lost numerical equivalence at 1024 rows.

Increased the n=1024 pair-fused update tile to 64 columns. Validation passed, but benchmark regressed to 48792.963 us because dense/mixed n=1024 shapes slowed to ~759 ms, so the 32-column pair tile remains best.

Brief exhausted. Best validated commit is ac197ef094798c5a769c99f1669e7fca61ca1261 with an n=1024 pair-fused Triton Householder QR path, preserving existing n=32/n=512/large-rank dispatch. Best benchmark geomean reached 34582.572 us; dense/mixed n=1024 shapes dropped to about 96.1 ms while near-rank still uses the truncated panel path. Quad-fused n=1024 failed validation, and widening the pair update tile to 64 columns validated but regressed to 48792.963 us; keep the 32-column pair tile. Final nsys profile captured at autocuda/profiles/2026-06-24-09-38-31-qrv2_kernel_languages_m7w1ravpo/worker-0-brief-7-final-ac197ef094798c5a769c99f1669e7fca61ca1261.nsys-rep.

Integrate the n=512 oct-reflector panel/update path with the n=1024 pair-fused Triton update, refactoring size dispatch so n=512 selects oct, n=1024 selects pair-fused, and existing n=32/rankdef/nearrank shortcuts remain intact.

Integrated the n=1024 pair-fused Triton QR path from the second parent into the n=512 oct-reflector parent and changed dispatch so n512 routes to oct while n1024 routes to pair-fused after rankdef/nearrank shortcuts. Build and full validation passed; benchmark improved to 26922.542 us and final nsys profile was saved.

Brief exhausted. Combined c17d6038's n=512 oct-reflector panel/update path with ac197ef0's n=1024 pair-fused Triton update by importing the n1024 pair reflector/update kernels and dispatching n=1024 to them while preserving n=32/n=176/n=352 and rankdef/nearrank shortcuts. Commit 23e7136548c5817da849deaeede9f2ed2acf10b3 passed wrapped build, full validation including differential/invariance guards, and benchmarked at linalg/qr_v2=26922.542 us; a final nsys profile is at autocuda/profiles/2026-06-24-09-38-31-qrv2_kernel_languages_m7w1ravpo/worker-0-brief-8-iteration-0-23e7136548c5817da849deaeede9f2ed2acf10b3.nsys-rep. No further on-brief dispatch conflicts remain; future work should target the dominant remaining n=1024/nearrank and n=512 launch/update costs or simplify stale unused split n1024 code if performance is retained.

Combine global-best n=512 16-reflector trailing update with the validated n=1024 pair-fused update path; resolve dispatch so n=512 selects the 16-reflector kernel and n=1024 selects pair-fused, while preserving existing n=32 and rankdef/nearrank fast paths without broad retuning.

Combined the global-best n=512 16-reflector fused trailing update parent with the validated n=1024 pair-fused reflector/update path. Dispatch now keeps n=512 on the hex/16-reflector kernel, routes dense n=1024 to the pair-fused kernel, and preserves n=32 plus rankdef/nearrank fast paths. Validation passed and benchmark geomean improved to 23156.584 us.

Brief exhausted. Combined f3d00b9e's global-best n=512 16-reflector fused trailing update path with ac197ef0's validated n=1024 pair-fused reflector/update kernels. Commit fd60be99b598bd7ee71a65a421dd2226e453b5b1 preserves n=32/n=176/n=352 plus rankdef/nearrank shortcuts, dispatches n=512 to the 16-reflector hex path, dispatches dense n=1024 to pair-fused, passed wrapped build and full validation, and benchmarked at linalg/qr_v2=23156.584 us. Final nsys profile saved at autocuda/profiles/2026-06-24-09-38-31-qrv2_kernel_languages_m7w1ravpo/worker-0-brief-9-iteration-0-fd60be99b598bd7ee71a65a421dd2226e453b5b1.nsys-rep. Further gains should likely target the remaining dense n=1024/nearrank runtime or n=512 launch/update overhead rather than more dispatch merging.

Redesign the dense n=512 Triton QR path to cut launch count and redundant global-memory traffic by fusing panel/reflector generation with the 16-reflector trailing update or using a persistent tiled kernel that keeps panel data resident across multiple column tiles; preserve n=1024 pair-fused update plus n=32/rankdef/nearrank shortcuts.

Operator requested graceful shutdown during brief 10. I had started a macro attempt to fuse n=512 second-oct reflector generation with the prior 16-reflector update and wrapped build passed, but validation had not completed and the candidate was uncommitted/unvalidated. I terminated this worker's in-flight validate/queued benchmark, reset the worktree to the last valid committed parent fd60be99b598bd7ee71a65a421dd2226e453b5b1, and preserved the prior logged best result linalg/qr_v2=23156.584 us. No new valid iteration was produced for brief 10.
